ai.description: Leith's Sand Snake reaches 1 meter in length. It is pale brown or sandy with a dark, light-edged vertebral stripe and a distinct dark streak through the eye. It has a slender body and large eyes.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Psammophis leithii* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark-edged pale stripe running along the center of its back, which is absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: Leith's Sand Snake inhabits arid and semi-arid rocky scrublands and sandy plains across the Indian subcontinent, typically at elevations below 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: Leith's Sand Snake is a diurnal hunter that actively pursues lizards and small rodents across rocky, arid landscapes with remarkable speed and agility.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Psammophis leithii* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 3–8 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: Leith's Sand Snake is endemic to the Indian subcontinent, primarily inhabiting the arid and semi-arid regions of peninsular India and parts of Pakistan.
